title: Processing devices
competency: Explain the CPU and its sub-components.

keywords.def: Central Processing Unit: the processor, the "brain" of the computer.
The part of the CPU that directs the other parts to carry out instructions.
Arithmetic Logic Unit: does arithmetic (+, −, ×, ÷) and logic comparisons (<, >, =).
A temporary storage place in the CPU for data waiting to be processed by the ALU.
The unit of processor speed: one cycle per second.

en.text: The Central Processing Unit (CPU), or processor, turns input data into useful information. It is the brain of the computer, and its speed is measured in hertz (one cycle per second). It has three parts joined by a bus. The control unit directs the other parts but does not carry out instructions itself. The arithmetic logic unit (ALU) does arithmetic and logic comparisons. Registers hold data temporarily before the ALU uses it.

screens.text: A school program checks "Is the student's average ≥ 50?" to decide pass or fail. Which unit does this and what kind of operation is it?
screens.why: Comparisons such as ≥ are logic operations, and the ALU performs them.
